I tried to track it down further, latest observations are that after upgrading `@angular/cli` to 1.5.0-beta.4 and `@ngtools/webpack` to 1.8.0-beta.4 the error changes.

5.0.0-rc.0 and 5.0.0-rc.1: Module not found: Error: Can't resolve './$$_gendir/code/application/application.module.ngfactory'
5.0.0-beta.7: No provider for NgForm error (known, see issue)
5.0.0-beta.6: Application compiles as expected

The apps code wasn't changed (not even a char) between the version switches, I can go back and forth and reproduce the error.
Will debug the app now as in the past all "module not found" errors where some odd things that I could resolve myself, albeit I'm wondering why it works in beta.6 but not rc.0/rc.1.

As far as I can tell by now, I think it's something inside `@angular/cli` or `@ngtools/webpack`, not `@angular/*` itself, so feel free to close the issue.
I'll keep you posted if there are any new observations when debugging.

I too am experiencing this error at work. 

We are using the following:

Node 8.9.0
Windows 10 x64

```

Cannot determine the module for class FullPage in /home/patrikx3/Projects/angular5/corifeus-web-material5/test/angular-webpack/angular/page/full-page.ts! Add FullPage to the NgModule to fix it.

Cannot determine the module for class Layout in /home/patrikx3/Projects/angular5/corifeus-web-material5/test/angular-webpack/angular/layout.ts! Add Layout to the NgModule to fix it.
test/angular-webpack/angular/bundle.aot.ts(8,9): error TS2305: Module '"/home/patrikx3/Projects/angular5/corifeus-web-material5/test/angular-webpack/angular/module.ngfactory"' has no exported member 'ModuleNgFactory'.
```

This should be supported but it appears the compiler is not handling the presence of the redundant `@Injectable()` on the module. A work around for this, until I submit a fix, is to remove `@Injectable()` from module classes. It might also be a good idea to remove the `@Injectable()` anywhere it is not the only Angular decorator.

issue.title: fix(compiler): recognize @NgModule with a redundant @Injectable

issue.body:
The compiler now, again, recognizes `@NgModule()` decorators on
classes with a redundant `@Injectable()` decorator.

Fixes: #19544

## PR Type
What kind of change does this PR introduce?

<!-- Please check the one that applies to this PR using "x". -->
```
[x] Bugfix
```

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number:  #19544

## What is the new behavior?

`ngc` will not recognize `@NgModule()` decorators on classes that have an `@Injectable()` decorator.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```

body:
Make sure the import path case matches with the actual file path case. I got the same error, for my MyUserComponent class shown below. Note the case of the import path (all the letters are in lower case).

`import { MyUserComponent } from './user/myusercomponent.component';`

The actual file name of MyUserComponent was

> myUserComponent.component.ts (note that U and C are in upper case)

Once I changed the import statement to the following
`import { MyUserComponent } from './user/myUserComponent.component';`
the error disappeared.

@anandmurali thanks for the tip, but this is not my issue. I am using a barrel file to import from so my paths are irrelevant, and I used the autocomplete feature in VS Code to make sure the paths are correct.
@lslocum Did you found any fix for this issue?
@HarshaVardhanPVK I was able to get a production APT build to work, but I don't remember how I resolved the issue. Sorry I couldn't be more of a help.
